packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-02 -- first blind reading (unverified image reading)

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001 overview, image-002 native)
- image-001: reduced overview. A very small fragment (approx. 6.5 x 5.5 cm by the ruler) on black ground, colour chart lower left, ruler at right. The fragment is a strip of parchment cut into four horizontal strips (three cuts), mounted together in a clear sleeve. A grey rectangle (redaction/label mask) covers part of the left half. A modern pencil note at lower left of the parchment reads "Stams, STA / Frag. 144x" (? last characters uncertain) - this is a shelfmark-type label, not text.
- image-002: native view of the same face. Only the right-hand edge carries writing: one column of a large Gothic textualis bookhand in brown ink, cut off at the right edge after 2-4 letters per line. To the left of the text is a blank margin (left two thirds of the fragment, no writing visible apart from the pencil note).
- Red (rubricated) decoration: a large red initial Q (bowl spanning ~2 lines, tail descending), then a large red initial (looks like a Q/G-form or S-form; bowl at the level of lines 3-4 with a long red vertical stroke/tail running down the left of the text to the bottom), and a red E (enlarged, ~1.5 lines) lower down. The long red stroke runs vertically along the left edge of the text block from line 4 to the bottom.
- Script size: large (letter height ~ 5 mm), suggesting a choir-book/liturgical-format hand, but this is only an interpretation. Line spacing very wide; possibly text underlaid for music, but no staves are visible in the surviving area (tentative).
- Lines visible: about 7 text lines (one partially cut at top), each reduced to the first few letters after the initial.
- Only one face is supplied (image-001/002). images 003/004 not yet viewed at time of writing this survey.

TRANSCRIPTION image-002 (one column, only line openings; right edge cut away)
Line numbers counted from top of image-002.
(read from image-002 with enlarged crop crop-01.jpg, right third of image-002)

image-002 l.1  [illegible: tops of letters only, cut by the upper edge; perhaps "...ag..." / "...ed..."]
image-002 l.2  [red initial Q]uo? [cut]    (red Q, then brown "uo", next letter cut at edge; "Quo" fairly secure, a further letter (d?) only as a trace)
image-002 l.3  [illegible traces below "uo", strip cut]
image-002 l.4  ...um? / iu? [cut]   (minims only, within the bowl area of the red letter; perhaps "um" or "iui")
image-002 l.5  [red letter lobe at left] nimu? / mmu? [cut]  (sequence of minims, faint; "nimu" or "unu" uncertain)
image-002 l.6  Et ideo [cut]   (capital E brown, "t" then "ideo"; clear)
image-002 l.7  [red initial E]go su? [cut]   ("Ego" secure; next letter long-s or f, then minims: "su" or "fu" uncertain)
image-002 l.8  ...mam in? / nam iu? [cut]   (lowest line, faint and cut by the lower edge of the fragment)

Red decoration notes: the large red form at lines 2-5 may be one initial Q with a lobe/tail continuing down, or two separate red initials (a Q at l.2-3 and another at l.4-5); the long thin red vertical line from l.5 to the bottom runs just left of the text and may be the tail of that initial or a ruling/penwork stroke. Uncertain.

LIMITATIONS
- Only line openings survive (2-7 letters per line); the right side of the column is cut away. No connected prose can be read on this face.
- Physical cuts between strips fall through lines 3 and 5/6 area; lines 1, 3, 8 are partly lost.
- Grey mask covers part of the left (blank) margin.

LAYOUT SURVEY, second face (image-003 overview)
- image-003: reduced overview of the other face of the same strip-mounted fragment (same four strips in a sleeve, pencil label visible through the sleeve at centre right, mirror side). Here the writing is at the LEFT edge: line endings of a column, with a red rubric word at about line 4 (reads at overview scale like "Iohem" with a following point). Brown text lines above and below. Right part blank margin with the label showing through. A faint red vertical stroke near the top centre (show-through of the red initial stroke from the other face, presumably).

LAYOUT, image-004 (native view of the second face)
- Same four-strip fragment. Pencil label through/on the sleeve reads "Stams, STA / Frag. 144v" (the "v" here is clear; on image-002 I wrote "144x" for the other face - that final character was uncertain and is presumably a different letter, likely "r"; I did not re-open image-002 to check).
- Writing only at the left edge: line ENDINGS of a column whose left part is cut away; the rest is blank margin. Same large Gothic textualis, brown ink, wide line spacing. Red show-through of the large initials from the other face is visible (pink blotches, mirror image) in the centre-left.
- One red rubric line (line 3 of this view). Enlarged-initial-like capital at line 1 with a red touch.

TRANSCRIPTION image-004 (read with crop-02.jpg, left ~40% of image-004 enlarged)
Line numbers counted from top of image-004. Left edge cut: text before what is shown is lost.

image-004 l.1  ·Q uae? [then blank]   (a capital - Q or D form - with a red vertical touch/stroke inside it, preceded by a point; then "uae" (or "nae"); a further faint letter/point after. Reading "Quae" or "·D· uae"? uncertain; I lean to "Quae". Tops of letters of a line above are visible at the very top edge, illegible)
image-004 l.2  ...tiuo? / ...ruo? [illegible, very faint, abraded]
image-004 l.3  [rubric, red:] ·Iohem·   (red; the "h" has a long descending tail; might be an abbreviated form (Ioh(ann)em ?) - no abbreviation stroke clearly seen; point before and after)
image-004 l.4  ...rlemu? / ...ulenu? (brown, upper half partly cut by the strip cut beneath it; letters "l e m/n u" fairly visible, first letter uncertain)
image-004 l.5  ...tinue? / ...rinne? / ...timu e   (brown; minims ambiguous: "t i n u e" is my best reading; final letter e)

Nothing else on this face carries text.

SUMMARY / LIMITATIONS
- Selected spans: all visible text on both faces (there is very little). Unread: nothing further visible; all remaining parchment area is blank margin (or masked by the grey rectangle on image-002).
- Face of image-002: only line OPENINGS survive (Quo..., Et ideo..., Ego su(?)...), with large red initials Q and E. Face of image-004: only line ENDINGS (...uae, rubric ...Iohem·, ...tinue?). Consistent with a strip from the inner/outer margin of a leaf in which the column runs off the cut edge.
- No connected prose (no span of 10 lines with continuous words) can be read; the fragment does not allow it.
- Minim sequences (um/nu/iui/in) cannot be resolved with confidence at the cut edges.

EXPOSURE / CONDUCT NOTES
- No proposed identification or prior reading was revealed in my context. The pencil label "Stams, STA Frag. 144v" is visible on the images themselves (shelfmark-type note, not an identification of the text).
- I ran `ls` on the packet directory restricted to *.jpg and `sips` to get image sizes and make two crops (crop-01.jpg, crop-02.jpg) in rscratch/packet-02. Nothing else opened.
